androidVersionShipped: 16 (community references to Infinity-X v3.9 / v3.10 QPR2 builds for cancunf; the exact current build must be confirmed on the official download page before install)
initialInstallPackageNotes: The cancunf-specific guide at cyberknight777.dev/instructions/cancunf/ and the DroidWin Android-16-ROM guide for G54/G64 both describe the same pattern: boot to fastbootd with 'adb reboot fastboot', flash the initial-install package with 'fastboot --skip-reboot update <package>.zip', then 'fastboot reboot recovery' and 'adb sideload <rom>.zip'. The exact initial-install package file name/version for the currently published Infinity-X build was not retrievable in this environment -- see verificationGapNotes.
dataFormatNotes: Moving from the stock Motorola firmware to an AOSP-derived custom ROM for the first time requires wiping /data (different filesystem encryption/format expectations). This is standard custom-ROM guidance, not cancunf-specific, and must still be reconfirmed on the official instructions page for the exact build used.
kernelSuNotes: KernelSU officially supports GKI 2.0 kernels (5.10+) with a matching KMI; a non-GKI or older kernel needs a manually built KernelSU kernel, which this app will not attempt to source or flash blindly. Whether the Infinity-X cancunf build ships a KernelSU-enabled kernel out of the box has not been confirmed -- VERIFY_KERNELSU_COMPATIBILITY must check the installed kernel's 'uname -r' string and the boot image itself (see KernelSuCompatibilityChecker) rather than assuming compatibility from the ROM's name or Android version.

verificationGapNotes: This build environment's network egress policy blocks direct retrieval of cyberknight777.dev, projectinfinity-x.com, and droidwin.com (HTTP 403 / DNS denial from the sandbox proxy -- an organization policy denial, not a transient error, and not evidence the pages themselves are down). As a result: the exact current Infinity-X build/version number, ZIP file name and size, published checksum and its algorithm, Initial Install package compatibility, and literal verbatim flashing commands for cancunf could NOT be confirmed first-hand in this environment and are deliberately left blank/null in this profile rather than invented. A 2026-10-10 web-search sweep additionally could not find independent confirmation that an Infinity-X build for cancunf exists at all (see citations) -- this does not prove it doesn't exist, but it means the user's locally downloaded ROM ZIP should not be assumed genuine Infinity-X/cancunf without the user personally opening https://projectinfinity-x.com/downloads/cancunf and cross-checking the exact filename, size and published checksum against the files in their AETHERIX_FILES folder. AETHERIX ROM MASTER's VERIFY_ROM and VERIFY_CHECKSUMS states will refuse to proceed past dry-run for this ROM profile until a human confirms the current build's instructions and checksum and updates this profile file (or supplies a checksum file alongside the downloaded ROM zip) -- consistent with the project rule to stop and explain rather than guess.
